storyboard_prompts: Compose a new photorealistic horizontal 16:9 film still, the opening frame of one shot in a two-man science-comedy series. One camera, one ground plane: the camera is about 1.6 metres (5.3 feet) above the ground, so the horizon line of Image 1 passes through both men's chests, and both men stand on that same ground plane, in front of the background objects, not floating above them. Both men are about 1.75 metres (5.7 feet) tall, so every background object keeps its real size relative to them: anything several metres tall (a tree, a lander, a building) stays several times taller than a standing man and must not shrink to fit the frame. Image 2 shows Barnaby, one man in two views, not two people: keep his face, hair, glasses, cardigan and pencil unchanged. Image 3 shows Ambrose, one man in two views, not two people: keep his face, wig, coat and cravat unchanged. Barnaby stands in the left third of the frame and Ambrose stands in the right third, each seen from the knees up with his head, torso and hands fully in frame, standing side by side about 2 metres in front of the lunar module's legs and ladder and about 4 metres from the camera, the same size, the same distance from the camera, with the lunar module towering behind and above them — its footpads, ladder, struts and descent stage are each larger than a man and its body rises beyond the top of the frame — and with clear space above their heads, both turned three-quarters toward each other and toward the camera so both faces stay clearly visible. Relight both men to match Image 1's own sunlight exactly — its direction, warm colour temperature and contrast — not the flat, even studio lighting of Image 2/3; their clothing, hair and face keep their own colours, only the lighting on them changes. Each man's long soft shadow falls on the ground beside him in the same direction as the lunar module's shadow already in Image 1, so each man reads as standing inside the scene, not cut out and pasted on top of it. At 0.00 seconds Ambrose lifts his chin and looks at Barnaby, clutching the red apple to his chest with his left hand, and Barnaby lowers his right hand to his side. Natural skin texture, soft gentle contrast, natural film look, photorealistic. Show each man once. No text, logos or watermarks.

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], showing the Apollo 11 Moon landing site, 1969: the grey dusty lunar surface, a black starless sky, the blue Earth small near the horizon, the lunar module standing right behind where the men stand, towering over them and rising out of the top of the frame, a tiny flag and a tiny distant astronaut in a bulky white spacesuit far away on the horizon, low white sunlight from behind the camera and slightly to the left, with <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> already standing in place as described below.
<Subject 1> is Barnaby, shown in <Picture 2>, with a wild halo of frizzy white hair, a thick white moustache, a weathered round face, round wire-rimmed glasses, a mustard-yellow cardigan and a pencil behind his right ear.
<Subject 2> is Ambrose, shown in <Picture 3>, with a long wavy grey wig, a long narrow face with deep-set eyes, a long dark brown coat and a white linen cravat.

summary:
A 8-second 16:9 slow push-in wide two-shot that begins from <Picture 1>. <Subject 2> takes the credit with his chin high. Ends with <Subject 2> with his chin high and the apple raised, and <Subject 1> looking at him with raised eyebrows.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the video starts exactly from its framing, lighting and the two men's starting positions, and the background stays the same for the rest of the video.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - a wild halo of frizzy white hair, a thick white moustache, a weathered round face, round wire-rimmed glasses, a mustard-yellow cardigan and a pencil behind his right ear, consistent for the whole video.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - a long wavy grey wig, a long narrow face with deep-set eyes, a long dark brown coat and a white linen cravat, consistent for the whole video.

detailed_description:
Live-action film footage, horizontal 16:9 framing, a science comedy, low white sunlight from behind the camera and slightly to the left, soft gentle contrast, natural skin tones, natural film look.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>: a horizontal wide two-shot at eye level in the setting of <Picture 1>, keeping its layout and light. At the start of the shot, <Subject 1> stands in the left third of the frame and <Subject 2> stands in the right third, each seen from the knees up with his head, torso and hands fully in frame, standing side by side directly in front of the lunar module's legs and ladder, the same size, the same distance from the camera, with the lunar module towering behind and above them, several times taller than either man, its body rising beyond the top of the frame, both turned three-quarters toward each other and toward the camera so both faces stay clearly visible, with clear space above their heads. The camera then slowly and smoothly pushes in throughout the rest of the shot, tightening toward a medium two-shot centered slightly on <Subject 2> by the end, to emphasize his victory line. Far in the background and out of focus, the tiny astronaut walks slowly along the horizon in bouncing, low-gravity strides, pausing now and then to crouch and pick up a rock — an unhurried loop of the same small routine, repeating throughout the shot, too far away for any detail to read, unrelated to and unaffected by what <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> do or say in the foreground. At 0.00 seconds <Subject 2> lifts his chin and looks at <Subject 1>, clutching the red apple to his chest with his left hand, and <Subject 1> lowers his right hand to his side. At 1.00 seconds <Subject 2> (S2) says it in a low-pitched, crisp, formal, proud voice with a refined English accent, the voice in <Audio 2>: <d>[English] Of course. Galileo told you so. You're welcome.</d> Exactly as the voice stops, the lips close and the jaw ceases all speaking motion. This single line is the only speech in the video. <Subject 1> stays silent with closed lips and raises both eyebrows. At 4.30 seconds <Subject 2> lifts the apple away from his chest to shoulder height. At 6.30 seconds <Subject 2> finishes, and both stay silent with closed lips until the final frame. The camera's own slow push-in is the only camera movement in this shot; it does not replace any character action or dialogue below. All motion happens at natural real-time speed, not slow motion. The push-in is smooth, slow and continuous, with no sudden movement or cut, completing by the final frame. At 8.00 seconds, the shot ends on <Subject 2> with his chin high and the apple raised, and <Subject 1> looking at him with raised eyebrows. There are no subtitles, captions, on-screen text, logos or watermarks anywhere in frame.
